title: Trace-anchored reuse mapper: sampling sprint notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes on a lightweight, trace-anchored reuse-mapper we ran to: (a) correct sampling bias in reuse-rate estimates, (b) surface eviction pathologies tied to memory-channel hotspots, and (c) measure paging read-amplification under different prefetch windows. Aim is experimental evidence for an adaptive pinning prototype.

Context / why: 
- Current KV telemetry undercounts long-tail reuse because sampling is weighted to hot keys and high-qps requests. We need a reproducible mapping from per-request traces -> per-key reuse histogram that is robust across seqlen mixes.
- Several customer incidents pointed to periodic NVMe storms correlated with eviction churn in multi-tenant pools. Suspect cross-request bank contention + poor eviction scoring.

What we built (sketch):
- Trace-anchored mapper: replay sampled request traces (N=10 production-mimic traces) with a shadow cache that records exact first/last access timestamps per key within the trace window.
- Lightweight hashing: use 64-bit key fingerprint to reduce memory of shadow cache, keep exact LRU stack position approximate via compact counter.
- Reservoir sampling layer: pick a uniform subset of requests across time buckets to avoid hot-time bias.
- Instrumentation hooks: per-evict decision log (score, reason code), per-spill event (nvme offset, async queue depth), memory BW clamps (per-channel counters exported from perf counters).

Experiment config: 
- HW: 4x A100-equivalent nodes, single NUMA domain per node for tests.
- Cache size: simulated resident set = 12GB (varied 6GB/12GB/18GB).
- Prefetch window candidates: 0 (disable), 8, 32, 128 tokens of lookahead.
- Eviction policies compared: lru, score-based (age+freq), bank-aware (score + bank-penalty), and pinned-seed prototype (pin top-K per-tenant).
- Traces: 10 traces from last 30 days, mix of chat (long seqlen) and single-shot completions. Seqlen distribution captured in metadata.

Key metrics we capture: 
- reuse_rate_per_key (median, p90, p99), reuse-length (delta between accesses), cold_miss_fraction, spillback_rate (requests that triggered nvme read), read_amplification = bytes_read_from_nvme / logical_tokens_served, eviction_decision_distribution (by reason code).
- memory_bandwidth_usage per channel (MB/s), queue_depths, read_latency_p50/p95/p99.

Findings (short):
1) Sampling bias matters: naive trace-sampling overestimates reuse by ~12% relative to uniform time-bucketed reservoir sampling. Hot bursts skew samples.
2) Bank-locality evaporation: when eviction policy ignores channel banking, nvme read-amplification increases 1.6x under mixed seqlen traces (long chat + short completions). Observed pattern: many evictions clustered on keys that, when paged back, map to same memory channel causing read queue amplification and tail latency spikes.
3) Prefetch window tradeoffs: small prefetch (8 tokens) reduced read_amplification by ~18% vs no-prefetch for long seqlen traces, but introduced CPU overhead and increased cold_miss_fraction for short completion traces. Bigger prefetch (128) helped throughput but increased memory BW saturation on channel 1 in our cluster; bank-aware prefetch gating is needed.
4) Pinning ROI: pin-top-K (K=512 per-tenant) reduced eviction churn for heavy tenants and lowered per-tenant p99 latency by ~22%, but naive pinning caused starvation for low-tenant footprints when resident set tight. Need soft pin (age-decay) or tenant-weighted pins.

Representative numbers (approx):
- median reuse rate (uniform sampling): 2.4, p95: 9.2, p99: 24.7
- naive sampling median: 2.7 (+12%), p99: 26.1
- read_amplification (no-prefetch, bank-unaware): 4.3x
- read_amplification (prefetch 8, bank-aware): 3.1x
- memory BW channel skew: channel0 520MB/s, channel1 1.9GB/s (imbalanced during eviction storms)

Profiles / traces to look at: 
- trace-07-longchat-heavy: shows repeated eviction of top-k shards causing NVMe microbursts; looking at per-evict logs shows score flips where age metric suddenly dominates frequency.
- trace-02-mix-short: small seqlen churn—prefetch window increases cold miss for tiny requests.

Hypotheses & lightweight models: 
- Hypothesis A: eviction scoring that includes a bank-penalty term (penalty proportional to estimated channel load) reduces read amplification and p99 by steering evictions across channels.
- Hypothesis B: reservoir sampling of requests combined with per-key lifespan capture yields stable reuse estimates that predict cache compression gains when enabling pinning.
- Empirical model: predicted p99 reduction = 0.7 * fraction_pinned - 0.25 * (resident_set_pressure) [very rough linear fit from 3 points].

Open questions / unknowns: 
- How well does bank-penalty generalize to different HW (PCIe topology differences)? Need cross-region replay on smaller EC2 machines.
- Can we cheaply estimate key->channel mapping in production without full shadowing? Maybe use low-overhead offline microbenchmarks to map fingerprint->bank probabilistically.
- Interaction with GPU-side KV caches (on-device KV): when both host and device caches present, eviction decisions must be coordinated. Haven't modeled that.

Immediate next experiments (TODOs):
- [ ] Run bank-aware eviction simulation across 3 different PCIe topologies (owner: Lena) -- target week of 2024-11-25.
- [ ] Implement reservoir sampler into production trace capture (Ravi) and validate reuse estimate drift over 30d.
- [ ] Prototype soft-pinning: pin with TTL and decay factor; test under multi-tenant burst mixes (Samantha).
- [ ] Add lightweight key->bank estimator: run fingerprint microbench and export mapping table (Marco).

Notes to self (fragments / raw):
- Prefetch=8 seems like a good default for chat-heavy workloads but must be gated by memory channel free headroom.
- Consider eviction hysteresis: penalize immediate re-evict of recently-evicted keys for T ms to avoid oscillation.
- Add per-tenant resident-set caps + burst buffer to prevent pins from starving others.
- Correlate p99 with nvme queue depth snapshots (strong correlation).

Artifacts attached (where):
- perf flamegraphs (s3://redwood-lab/reuse-mapper/20241107/trace07-flame.svg)
- CSV export of per-key reuse histograms (s3 link in JIRA ticket INF-2897)
- notebook: sandbox/reuse-mapper-explore.ipynb (local)

Suggested decisions for product/ops: 
- We should ship bank-aware eviction as experimental flag in Dedicated (behind runtime flag) before enabling in Hosted. Justification: low-risk, measurable p99 improvements and prevents NVMe storms.
- Proposal: default prefetche window 8 for chat-optimized models, but auto-scale/disable when measured channel BW > 70% of advertised.

If we want to turn experimental work into a small RFC: include the sampling-correction method, bank-penalty formula, and soft-pin TTL semantics. Keep the telemetry hooks minimal (per-evict reason + bank-id + read-amplification windows).

Open followups:
- Validate the reservoir sampler on 60-day traces to ensure no seasonality bias.
- Measure impact of soft-pin on tail for tiny tenants.
- Decide instrumentation footprint allowed in production (max 5% CPU overhead budget).

End notes. This is a scratchpad; copy good bits to an RFC when stable.
